Alex: Heads up — after the paged-alloc-refactor merge we're seeing a p99 decode latency regression on the large-chat workload in prod. I rolled the service back but want to trace root cause.
Priya: Ugh. Can you paste the perf numbers and the canary config? :eyes:
Alex: p50 12ms -> 14ms, p95 38ms -> 46ms, p99 42ms -> 98ms after the roll. Canary config: `pager.eviction_threshold=0.6`, `pager.alloc_strategy=slab`, batcher defaults.
Simon: Any flame or perf samples? Could be blocktable scan in the KV pager now that allocator layout changed.
Priya: I ran a quick perf on a repro VM. Top stack (sampling):
```
  24% kv_pager::find_free_block
  18% blocktable::scan_range
  12% slotmap::reclaim_slot
   9% attn_kernel::pagewalk
   6% cudaMemcpyAsync
```
Priya: Means we're spending time scanning blocktable entries when fragmentation is high — cost is linear in number of blocks probed.
Rachel: That matches my local microbench. The new slab layout reduced metadata locality, so hot prefix hits now trigger more full-table scans. FlashV2 fallback also seems to pick a different kernel when batch sizes vary which interacts badly.
Jon: Also check the batching heuristics: if batcher coalesces very uneven sequence lengths we'll get larger KV cache churn and more cross-chunk evictions. I have a load test that reproduces this with seqlen skew.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: reverted service/inference to r1.1.14 (was r1.2.0-canary) — CI: green :white_check_mark:
Alex: Thanks. Hypothesis: slab alloc with 64KB chunk units + fragmented free list leads to high probe counts on allocation path. When many small requests churn KV pages we scan a lot.
Priya: Proposed mitigations to try in canary:
- switch `pager.alloc_strategy=hybrid` (segregated lists for small/large)
- bump `pager.slab_chunk_size=16k` for small-tier
- add fast-path: `blocktable.indexed_lookup` for >32k blocks
I can bench these in a microbench tomorrow.
Simon: Also add runtime telemetry (console) for `kv.pager.block_scans`, `kv.pager.alloc_ms`, `kv.pager.evictions` aggregated per-minute. That'll tell us if scans spike during the regressions.
Rachel: And emit `attn.kernel_selected` + `batch_size` so we can correlate kernel switches with pager churn.
Jon: I ran microbench: linear scan vs index lookup on 100k blocks, ops/sec: linear=1.1k, indexed=6.8k. Latency p99 linear=120ms, indexed=18ms. Sketch: https://gist.mock/kv-block-index-bench
Alex: I'll flip `pager.alloc_strategy=hybrid` and enable the telemetry in a canary ramp. If we still see p99 > 70ms I'll open a follow-up with the bench numbers and a perf trace.
Priya: One more note — kernel selection fallback logic currently probes kernel runtime with a cold KV hit. If we add a small warmup for kernel selection (sample a few tokens first) it avoids the pathological path that triggers extra pagewalks.
Alex: Good call. I'll prototype a warmup flag `attn.kernel_warmup_samples=8` in the canary too.
Simon: If you want me to land the telemetry PR I can — will add dashboards for the new metrics.
Alex: Please do. Thanks everyone — will post canary results here.
